issues.description: The Person class in the solution repository declares the first-name field as 'forename' but its getters/setters and other methods refer to 'firstName'. The template and tests use 'firstName'. This name mismatch inside the solution's Person class causes a structural inconsistency that will lead to compile errors and prevents tests and other code from interacting with the field as intended.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the field name consistent across the codebase. Rename the 'forename' field in the solution's Person class to 'firstName' (or update all getters/setters, equals, hashCode, and tests to use 'forename') so that the field name matches the template, tests, and all method references.

issues.description: The Person entity's first-name attribute is named inconsistently across artifacts: the template and tests use the identifier 'firstName' (with corresponding getters/setters and test calls to setFirstName/getFirstName), while the solution's Person class declares the field as 'forename'. This mismatch breaks the clear conceptual mapping between the problem (working with Person.firstName), the provided template, and the reference solution, and may confuse students about which identifier to use and where the data is stored.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier for the person's given name consistent across all artifacts. Rename the field 'forename' in the solution's Person class to 'firstName' (and keep/get/update the existing getFirstName/setFirstName methods), or alternatively rename the field and all usages in template, tests, and problem description to 'forename' so every reference uses the same identifier. Prefer aligning the solution to the template/tests by using 'firstName'.
